name: Merge a pull request
definition: The ability for an authorized actor to integrate the changes proposed by an already-open, non-draft pull request into its target branch, subject to the repository's own merge policies, producing a definitive merged/closed outcome or an identifiable failure reason.
capabilityPurpose: Enable the changes proposed by an open pull request to be incorporated into the target branch, using one of a small set of documented merge strategies, once the repository's own conditions for merging are satisfied.

includes: Choosing (or accepting a default for) the merge strategy: merge commit, squash, or rebase
Optionally overriding the automatic commit title/message
Optionally requiring the head branch to match a specific commit before merging, as a safety check
The immediate success/failure outcome of the merge attempt itself
excludes: Opening the pull request being merged -- a separate Capability MLE with a different actor and timing
Reviewing/approving the pull request -- governed by separate review mechanisms (pull_request_review) that this capability's policies may depend on, but do not themselves perform
Closing a pull request without merging -- a distinct, separately documented operation (state: closed via the update operation), not the merge endpoint

Enabling or disabling auto-merge (merging automatically once conditions are later satisfied) -- a distinct, separately documented set of webhook actions and CLI flag whose immediate effect is 'schedule a future merge,' not 'merge now'; excluded from this run's scope as a deliberate choice, not a GitHub-documented boundary
Checking whether a pull request has already been merged -- a distinct, separately documented read-only operation
Updating a pull request's branch with the latest base-branch changes -- a distinct, separately documented operation

Configuring branch protection itself (required reviews, required status checks, required linear history) -- those are policies this capability's contract is subject to, not actions this capability performs
Merging a draft pull request: GitHub's docs state you can't merge a draft pull request

meaningfulOutcome: The pull request becomes merged (target branch now contains the proposed changes; response confirms merged: true), or the attempt is rejected with an identifiable reason (forbidden, not found, merge not currently possible, head-SHA mismatch, or validation failure).

interactionContracts.name: Merge a pull request
interactionContracts.actor: A repository member holding the Write, Maintain, or Admin repository role (or an actor whose access is otherwise elevated) -- Read and Triage roles cannot merge.
interactionContracts.commandIntent: Integrate the pull request's proposed commits into its base branch using a specified or repository-permitted merge method, optionally supplying a commit title/message and a head-SHA precondition.
interactionContracts.currentState: An open, non-draft pull request exists. Its mergeable/mergeable_state may or may not currently be clean, depending on branch protection and conflict status; the full set of possible mergeable_state values is not documented in the material fetched.

policiesInvariants.text: The actor must hold Write, Maintain, or Admin repository access (or bypass rights).
A draft pull request cannot be merged.

If the target branch requires reviews, collaborators can only merge via a pull request approved by the required number of reviewers; pending or rejected reviews produce an error message on merge attempt.
If the target branch requires status checks, all required status checks must reach successful, skipped, or neutral status before a merge can succeed.
If the target branch requires linear history, only squash or rebase merges are permitted (merge commits are blocked).

By default, branch-protection restrictions do not apply to actors with admin permissions or an explicit bypass-branch-protections role; an organization may choose to apply the restrictions to them as well.
If sha is supplied, it must match the pull request's current head commit, or the merge fails with 409.
merge_method, when supplied, must be one of merge, squash, or rebase; no documented default value for this parameter was found.

interactionContracts.transition: Open, non-draft pull request (mergeable state permitting) to merged pull request; the pull request's state also becomes closed as a result of merging.
interactionContracts.result: On success (200): sha (resulting merge commit SHA), merged: true, and a message. On failure: 403 Forbidden; 404 Not Found; 405 Method Not Allowed if merge cannot be performed; 409 Conflict if sha was provided and pull request head did not match; 422 validation failed or the endpoint has been spammed.
eventsEffects: pull_request webhook event with action: closed

GitHub's REST pull-request resource carries a merged boolean field distinguishing a merge from a plain close (reasonable inference for its role specifically inside the closed webhook payload, as opposed to only the REST resource schema)
Notifications to other users/systems, subject to secondary rate limiting
unknowns: The full enumeration and meaning of mergeable_state values
Whether the webhook closed payload's own description text ties merged to that action
Whether a default merge_method is applied when the parameter is omitted
The precise conditions that distinguish a 405 from a 422 failure

rulesInvariants.text: Only actors with Write, Maintain, or Admin repository access (or explicit bypass rights) may merge a pull request.
A draft pull request cannot be merged.
Required reviews, if configured, must be satisfied before a merge can succeed.
Required status checks, if configured, must reach a successful/skipped/neutral state before a merge can succeed.
Required linear history, if configured, restricts the permitted merge_method to squash or rebase.
If sha is supplied, it must match the pull request's current head commit, or the merge fails with 409.

recommendedDefaults.text: By default, branch-protection restrictions (required reviews/status checks) do not apply to actors with admin permissions or an explicit bypass-branch-protections role.
The web UI's plain merge button uses a merge commit with --no-ff; whether the REST API's merge_method parameter shares an equivalent unstated default is unknown/unresolved.
Optionally deleting the head branch after a successful merge is a convenience, not a requirement.

unknowns: The full set of mergeable_state values and what each one means
Whether the webhook payload's own documentation explicitly states that pull_request.merged distinguishes a closed-via-merge outcome from a plain close
Whether a default merge_method is applied by the REST/GraphQL API when the parameter is omitted
The precise, general conditions that distinguish a 405 from a 422 failure
Whether GitHub Actions workflows or other bot tokens can be the actor for this capability under the general Write/Maintain/Admin rule

Whether any third-party GitHub-native bot is documented as ever merging (as opposed to only opening) a pull request -- Dependabot pull requests are documented as manually reviewed and merged by the user

communicationMLEs.purpose: Confirm to the actor or calling system that requested the merge that it completed, and identify the resulting commit.
